arxiv-1905-08877.title: Complete Positivity for Mixed Unitary Categories
arxiv-1905-08877.creator: Robin Cockett, Priyaa Varshinee Srinivasan
arxiv-1905-08877.description: Abstract Coecke and Heunen described completely positive maps in dagger monoidal categories and the CP -infinity construction on these categories in order to construct a category of arbitrary dimensional quantum processes. This article generalizes the 𝖢𝖯 \mathsf{CP} -infinity construction of dagger monoidal categories to mixed unitary categories.

arxiv-2105-04403.title: Alexander Arhangel’skii
arxiv-2105-04403.creator: Ol’ga Sipacheva
arxiv-2105-04403.description: Abstract . This is the opening article of the abstract book of conference “Set-Theoretic Topology and Topological Algebra” in honor of professor Alexander Arhangelskii on the occasion of his 80th birthday held in 2018 at Moscow State University. A good mathematician … never grows old. He remains a child. He remains a dreamer: curious, imaginative, free of concrete purpose.

arxiv-2106-10324.title: Group-Structured Adversarial Training Thanks: Laboratory for Information & Decision Systems, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, email: farnia@mit.edu Thanks: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, University of California, Berkeley, email: amiralia@berkeley.edu Thanks: Depart
arxiv-2106-10324.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . Robust training methods against perturbations to the input data have received great attention in the machine learning literature. A standard approach in this direction is adversarial training which learns a model using adversarially-perturbed training samples. However, adversarial training performs suboptimally against perturbations structured across samples such as universal and group-sparse shifts that are commonly present in biological data such as gene expression levels of different tissues.

arxiv-2108-11105.title: Lightweight Monocular Depth with a Novel Neural Architecture Search Method
arxiv-2108-11105.creator: Lam Huynh 1 Phong Nguyen 1 Jiri Matas 2 Esa Rahtu 3 Janne Heikkilä 1 1 Center for Machine Vision and Signal Analysis, University of Oulu 2 Center for Machine Perception, Czech Technical University, Czech Republic 3 Computer Vision Group, Tampere University
arxiv-2108-11105.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel neural architecture search method, called LiDNAS, for generating lightweight monocular depth estimation models. Unlike previous neural architecture search (NAS) approaches, where finding optimized networks is computationally highly demanding, the introduced novel Assisted Tabu Search leads to efficient architecture exploration.

arxiv-2201-06770.title: Storm Surges as Seen by Coastal and Spaceborne Radars: Case Studies in British Columbia
arxiv-2201-06770.creator: Baptiste Domps, Charles-Antoine Guérin
arxiv-2201-06770.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Baptiste Domps, Charles-Antoine Guérin. Short-term sea level fluctuations prompted by abrupt atmospheric changes can be hazardous phenomena for coastal regions. We report on two such recent storm surges that occurred in 2020 on the shores of British Columbia, Canada. A rare concordance of ground-based and spaceborne sensors made it possible to observe these events with a variety of instruments : (1) a coastal oceanographic radar; (2) the synthetic aperture radar onboard satellite Sentinel-1B; and (3) a network of shoreside tide gauges.

arxiv-2207-07559.title: Polyhedral approximations of Riemannian manifolds
arxiv-2207-07559.creator: Anton Petrunin
arxiv-2207-07559.description: Abstract We give a condition on the curvature tensors of Riemannian manifolds that admit Lipschitz approximation by polyhedral metrics with curvature bounded below or above. We show that this condition is also sufficient for the existence of local approximations. We conjecture that it is also sufficient for the global approximations and prove it in some special cases.

arxiv-2210-10663.title: A Review of Data-Driven Discovery for Dynamic Systems
arxiv-2210-10663.creator: Joshua S. North, Christopher K. Wikle, Erin M. Schliep
arxiv-2210-10663.description: Abstract Many real-world scientific processes are governed by complex nonlinear dynamic systems that can be represented by differential equations. Recently, there has been increased interest in learning, or discovering, the forms of the equations driving these complex nonlinear dynamic system using data-driven approaches. In this paper we review the current literature on data-driven discovery for dynamic systems.

arxiv-2309-13207.title: Evidential Deep Learning: Enhancing Predictive Uncertainty Estimation for Earth System Science Applications
arxiv-2309-13207.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . Robust quantification of predictive uncertainty is critical for understanding factors that drive weather and climate outcomes. Ensembles provide predictive uncertainty estimates and can be decomposed physically, but both physics and machine learning ensembles are computationally expensive. Parametric deep learning can estimate uncertainty with one model by predicting the parameters of a probability distribution but do not account for epistemic uncertainty.

arxiv-2405-18443.title: Using Thermal Crowding to Direct Pattern Formation on the Nanoscale
arxiv-2405-18443.creator: Ryan Allaire, Linda J. Cummings, Lou Kondic
arxiv-2405-18443.description: Abstract Metal films and other geometries of nanoscale thickness, when exposed to laser irradiation, melt and evolve as fluids as long as their temperature is sufficiently high. This evolution often leads to pattern formation, which may be influenced strongly by material parameters that are temperature dependent. In addition, the laser heat absorption itself depends on the time-dependent metal thickness.

arxiv-2412-17688.title: Refining the Two-Band Model for Highly Compensated Semimetals Using Thermoelectric Coefficients
arxiv-2412-17688.creator: Ian A. Leahy †, Andrew C. Treglia ‡, Gang Cao, Brian J. Skinner, Minhyea Lee
arxiv-2412-17688.description: Abstract In studying compensated semimetals, the two-band model has proven extremely useful in capturing electrical conductivity under magnetic field, as a function of density and mobility of electron-like and hole-like carriers. However, it rarely offers practical insight into magneto-thermoelectric properties.

arxiv-2501-15096.title: Towards Better Robustness: Pose-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting for Arbitrarily Long Videos
arxiv-2501-15096.creator: Zhen-Hui Dong, Sheng Ye, Yu-Hui Wen, Nannan Li, Yong-Jin Liu
arxiv-2501-15096.description: Abstract . 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a powerful representation due to its efficiency and high-fidelity rendering. 3DGS training requires a known camera pose for each input view, typically obtained by Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines. Pioneering works have attempted to relax this restriction but still face difficulties when handling long sequences with complex camera trajectories.

arxiv-2506-05995.title: Anomalous flow in correlated quantum systems: No-go result and multiple-charge scenario
arxiv-2506-05995.creator: Rui Guan, Junjie Liu
arxiv-2506-05995.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rui Guan, Junjie Liu. Correlated quantum systems can exhibit thermodynamic behaviors that defy classical expectations, with anomalous energy flow (AEF) against temperature gradients serving as a paradigmatic example. While AEF has been shown to arise from the consumption of initial quantum correlations, little is known about whether AEF can occur without correlation depletion, or if analogous anomalous transport exists for conserved charges beyond energy. Here, we develop a general global-local thermodynamic approach to describe charge exchange between arbitrary correlated quantum systems.

arxiv-2507-05895.title: Topped baryons from QCD sum rules
arxiv-2507-05895.creator: Shu-Wei Zhang, Wei-Han Tan, Xuan Luo, Hua-Xing Chen
arxiv-2507-05895.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shu-Wei Zhang, Wei-Han Tan, Xuan Luo, Hua-Xing Chen. The recent CMS observation of a near-threshold enhancement in top quark pair production CMS:2025kzt provides the first experimental indication of a short-lived pseudoscalar t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} bound state, commonly referred to as toponium . While most existing studies focus on toponium using perturbative QCD near threshold, baryonic configurations containing a single top quark— singly topped baryons —offer a complementary nonperturbative perspective.

arxiv-2508-01768.title: “Energon”: Unveiling Transformers from GPU Power and Thermal Side-Channels
arxiv-2508-01768.creator: Arunava Chaudhuri 1 , Shubhi Shukla 2 , Sarani Bhattacharya 1 , and Debdeep Mukhopadhyay 1
arxiv-2508-01768.description: Abstract Transformers have become the backbone of many Machine Learning (ML) applications, including language translation, summarization, and computer vision. As these models are increasingly deployed in shared Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) environments via Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS), concerns around their security grow.

arxiv-2510-11919.title: LLM Reasoning for Machine Translation: Synthetic Data Generation over Thinking Tokens
arxiv-2510-11919.creator: Armel Zebaze, Rachel Bawden & Benoît Sagot
arxiv-2510-11919.description: Abstract Large reasoning models (LRMs) have led to new possibilities in terms of problem-solving, through the devising of a natural language thought process prior to answering a query. While their capabilities are well known across mathematics and coding tasks, their impact on the task of machine translation (MT) remains underexplored.

plos-pone-0002948.title: Intriguing Balancing Selection on the Intron 5 Region of LMBR1 in Human Population
plos-pone-0002948.creator: Fang He, Dong-Dong Wu, Qing-Peng Kong et al.
plos-pone-0002948.description: PLOS ONE research article. The intron 5 of gene LMBR1 is the cis-acting regulatory module for the sonic hedgehog ( SHH ) gene. Mutation in this non-coding region is associated with preaxial polydactyly, and may play crucial roles in the evolution of limb and skeletal system. We sequenced a region of the LM

plos-pone-0005822.creator: Ethan E. Mann, Kelly C. Rice, Blaise R. Boles et al.
plos-pone-0005822.description: PLOS ONE research article. Recent studies have demonstrated a role for Staphylococcus aureus cidA -mediated cell lysis and genomic DNA release in biofilm adherence. The current study extends these findings by examining both temporal and additional genetic factors involved in the control of genomic DNA rele

pmc-10514621.title: Study within a trial of electronic versus paper-based Patient-Reported oUtcomes CollEction (SPRUCE): study protocol for a partially randomised patient preference study
pmc-10514621.creator: Lara Philipps, Stephanie Foster, Deborah Gardiner, Jacqui Gath, Alexa Gillman, Joanne Haviland, Elizabeth Hill, Diana King, Georgina Manning, Morgaine Stiles, Emma Hall, Rebecca Lewis
pmc-10514621.description: IntroductionPatient-reported outcomes (PRO) are currently collected from trial participants using paper questionnaires by the Clinical Trials and Statistics Unit at The Institute of Cancer Research (ICR-CTSU). Streamlining PRO collection using electronic questionnaires (ePRO) may improve data collection and patient experience.

pmc-11393353.title: Increased risk of depression and associated symptoms in poststroke aphasia
pmc-11393353.creator: Shih-Kai Kao, Chia-Ta Chan
pmc-11393353.description: Poststroke aphasia hinders patients’ emotional processing and social adaptation. This study estimated the risks of depression and related symptoms in patients developing or not developing aphasia after various types of stroke. Using data from the US Collaborative Network within the TriNetX Diamond Network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults experiencing their first stroke between 2013 and 2022.

pmc-11572390.title: NAMAH—An Innovative Tele-ECHO Mentoring Program to Foster Well-being Among Physicians
pmc-11572390.creator: Nidhi Parate, Manjunatha BR, Sanchitha R, Venkata Lakshmi Narasimha, Jayant Mahadevan, Prabhat Chand, Pratima Murthy, Sanjeev Arora
pmc-11572390.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background:The current study aimed to develop and implement the National Assistance in Mental Health for Health Care Providers (NAMAH) module, which focused on wellness and building resilience for a cohort of physicians.Methods:The NAMAH module is a 12-week tele-mentoring program leveraging videoconference technology that uses the ECHO (Extension of Community Healthcare Outcome) HUB and SPOKE and consists of real-life case discussions and a brief didactic.

pmc-11624680.title: Recent Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Discovery of New Antibacterial Agents
pmc-11624680.creator: Youcef Bagdad, Maria A Miteva
pmc-11624680.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents today a major challenge for global public health, compromising the effectiveness of treatments against a multitude of bacterial infections. In recent decades, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising technology for the identification and development of new antibacterial agents. This review focuses on AI methodologies applied to discover new antibacterial candidates.

pmc-11686226.title: Naoqing formula alleviates acute ischaemic stroke-induced ferroptosis via activating Nrf2/xCT/GPX4 pathway
pmc-11686226.creator: Yujun Ye, Xuexin Xie, Yiming Bi, Qing Liu, Xuliang Weng, Lingling Qiu, He Zhao, Shangyan Hei, Ling Yang, Chengyin Wang, Weifeng Zhu, Ting Zeng
pmc-11686226.description: BackgroundsFerroptosis is a form of regulated cell death. The accumulation of iron in the brain is linked to trigger ferroptosis after an ischaemic stroke (IS). Naoqing formula (NQ) is a traditional Chinese medicine metabolites with the clinical function of activating blood circulation, which is applied to treat IS clinically in China.

pmc-12500936.title: Enhanced spatiotemporal skeleton modeling: integrating part-joint attention with dynamic graph convolution
pmc-12500936.creator: Yanghong Qin, Shengrui Liu, Chunhong Yuan
pmc-12500936.description: Human motion prediction and action recognition are critical tasks in computer vision and human-computer interaction, supporting applications in surveillance, robotics, and behavioral analysis. However, effectively capturing the fine-grained semantics and dynamic spatiotemporal dependencies of human skeleton movements remains challenging due to the complexity of coordinated joint and part-level interactions over time.

pmc-12780440.title: Association between eosinophil counts and outcomes of severe coronavirus disease 2019 in elderly asthma patients: a prospective cohort study
pmc-12780440.creator: Sergey N. Avdeev, Viliya V. Gaynitdinova, Svetlana Y. Chikina, Zamira M. Merzhoeva, Galiya S. Nuralieva, Tatiana Y. Gneusheva, Elizaveta S. Sokolova, Tamara U. Bogatyreva, Zelimkhan G. Berikkhanov, Qingyun Ma
pmc-12780440.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundGiven effects of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection on the respiratory system and epidemiological burden of asthma worldwide, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in asthma patients caused reasonable concern to be a “dangerous” combination in early pandemic. This is especially pertinent to elderly patients with asthma since older age, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension, is associated with more serious complications of COVID-19 and higher mortality.

pmc-13079596.title: Neurobiological insights into perinatal depression: a multi-dimensional integration of brain structure, function, and metabolism
pmc-13079596.creator: Yue Sun, Lanqing Liu, Chaozhi Bu, Minhui Jiang, Xiaomin Zheng
pmc-13079596.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivePerinatal depression (PND) represents a significant challenge to maternal and infant health. In recent years, the rapid advancement of neuroimaging techniques has offered critical insights for elucidating the neurobiological mechanisms underlying PND.

pmc-13168232.title: Overcoming multidrug resistance Acinetobacter baumanii via downregulated virulence factor genes by green fabricated silver Nanoparticles mediated Piper nigrum
pmc-13168232.creator: Bassam Shaker Mahmood, Yasser Ali Hussein, Hind Majid Ahmed, Anwer Jaber Faisal, Majid S Jabir, Bakr Ahmed Taha, Suresh Ghotekar, Balamuralikrishnan Balasubramanian, Ayman A Swelum
pmc-13168232.description: Acinetobacter baumannii is a well-known pathogen that causes both community-acquired infections and nosocomial infections, particularly pneumonia associated with the use of ventilators. Numerous virulence factors and strong genomic plasticity are reported to be present in this opportunistic pathogen, which help it succeed in the infectious process.

pmc-13255871.title: Genetic Diversity and Population Structure Among Czech and Polish Goat Breeds Assessed Using Microsatellite Markers
pmc-13255871.creator: Zuzana Sztankóová, Emil Krupa, Emilia Bagnicka, Paulina Nazar, Monika Gregula Kania, Jana Rychtářová
pmc-13255871.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryMolecular characterization of local breeds is a key factor in biodiversity conservation. It should be combined with appropriate breeding strategies to improve the production characteristics of indigenous breeds and prevent breed decline. In this study, we analyzed 398 animals from eight goat breeds (White Shorthaired goat, Brown Shorthaired goat, Alpine, Anglo-Nubian, Polish White Improved goat, Polish Fawn Improved goat, Sandomierska, Toggenburg) bred in the Czech Republic and Poland using 15 microsatellite loci. All microsatellite markers were polymorphic.
